subject: sentences
title: To, Two or Too?
about: Words that sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things: to, two, too; there, their; see, sea; hear, here; one, won; new, knew; write, right; ate, eight; blue, blew; sun, son. The voice says the sentence with the word in it and he picks the spelling that fits the meaning: NC L.1.4 unpacks word relationships as synonyms, antonyms and homophones, while choosing the right spelling (L.1.2) is a step ahead of first grade, so read the choices with him at first.
tip: Have him read the sentence with each spelling and ask what it would mean: is it the number two, or going to the park?

cards.sayQ: I have two cats. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Two is the number 2. To tells where you go, and too means also.

cards.sayQ: We went to the park. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: To tells where you go. Two is the number 2.

cards.sayQ: I want to go too! Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Too means also: me too. It has an extra o, like an extra person coming along.

cards.sayQ: Your hat is over there. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: There tells a place, like here. Their means it belongs to them.

cards.sayQ: Mia and Ben walk their dog. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Their means it belongs to them. There tells a place.

cards.sayQ: I see a red bird. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: See is what your eyes do. The sea is the big salty water.

cards.sayQ: The boat is on the sea. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: The sea is the big water a boat floats on. See is what your eyes do.

cards.sayQ: Can you hear the bell? Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Hear has the word ear inside it. You hear with your ear. Here means this place.

cards.sayQ: Come here and sit down. Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Here means this place, like there. Hear is what your ears do.

cards.sayQ: Zoe won the race! Pick the spelling that fits.
cards.note: Won means she came in first. One is the number 1.

cards.sayQ: I have one cat. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: One is the number 1. Won is what you did when you came in first.

cards.sayQ: Max got new shoes. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: New means not old. Knew means you already had it in your head.

cards.sayQ: Liv knew the answer. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: Knew is the past of know: she knew it already. The k is silent.

cards.sayQ: I can write my name. Which way is it spelled here?
cards.note: Write is what you do with a pencil. The w is silent. Right means correct, or the side across from left.

cards.sayQ: Wave your right hand. Which spelling fits?
cards.note: Right is the side across from left. Write is what you do with a pencil.

cards.sayQ: A spider has eight legs. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: Eight is the number 8. Ate means you had some food.

cards.sayQ: The wind blew my hat off. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: Blew is the past of blow: the wind blew. Blue is a color.

cards.sayQ: Dad has one son, Ben. Which one is the right spelling?
cards.note: A son is a boy child. The sun is the hot star in the sky.
